title: Situation One
context: An intern from Canada just arrived at your company and your boss wants the team to say hello and introduce themselves to him.
minorCanDo: Get to know Alex and introduce yourself. Alex will ask a few questions and you must answer them.

classPlan.goal: Build the language toolkit (greetings, self-intro, to be, a/an)
Controlled → freer practice, ending in pair role-play
Live simulated first meeting with Alex, checklist-assessed

blocks.label: Student's book
blocks.body: **Situation One:** An intern from Canada just arrived at your company and your boss wants the team to say hello and introduce themselves to him.

blocks.label: Analyze the situation
items: Who is Alex? Why is he at your company?
Your boss is watching. Is this moment **formal**, **casual**, or something in between?
Prediction: write **3 questions** you think Alex will ask you.
Have you ever met a foreign colleague or client? What did you say?

blocks.title: Culture note — meeting a Canadian at work
blocks.body: First names are normal (call him Alex, not Mr. Alex), a smile + handshake is enough, and small talk is expected. "How's it going?" is a greeting, not a real question — the answer is short: *"Good, thanks! And you?"*

teacherNotes: Anticipated problem: students treat 'How's it going?' as a real question → drill the short-answer reflex before they predict Alex's questions.
Full Alex profile lives on the Can Do Proof slide — skim it beforehand so predicted questions stay realistic (A1-level, friendly interlocutor).

slides.goal: Rehearse the greeting reflex before meeting Alex

blocks.label: Board it together
blocks.body: **Alex walks in.** What is the *very first thing* you say? Call it out — we'll write the best openers on the board.

blocks.label: Quick drill
blocks.body: Alex says *"How's it going?"* — you have **two seconds** to answer. Don't overthink it: *"Good, thanks! And you?"*

teacherNotes: Keep this fast and on your feet — it's the bridge into the vocabulary slide, not a full activity.
If students freeze on the short-answer reflex, model it twice and move on.

slides.goal: Build the language toolkit (greetings, self-intro, to be, a/an)

columns.title: Phrase
rows: Welcome to the team! / Welcome aboard!
Nice to meet you. → Nice to meet you too!
How's it going? / How are you? → Good, thanks! And you?

columns.title: Phrase
rows: I'm on the `___` team / I work in `___`

columns.title: Example
rows: *I'm on the mobile team. I work in design.*
*I'm from Chapecó, in the south of Brazil.*

blocks.label: C. Keeping the conversation going
items: **What about you? / And you?** — return the question
**Where are you from in Canada?**
**Is this your first time in Brazil?**
**Are you here for long?**

blocks.label: D. Closing politely
items: **It was nice meeting you!**
**See you around! / Talk soon!**
**If you need anything, just ask.**

blocks.label: Grammar box — Verb "to be"
blocks.note: ⚠️ Age uses *to be*, not *have*: **I'm 28 years old.** (never ~~I have 28 years~~)

blocks.title: Footnote — Articles "a / an"
blocks.body: Use **a** before a consonant *sound*, **an** before a vowel *sound*: *a developer, a designer, a manager* — *an intern, an engineer, an accountant*. No article before names and cities: *I'm ~~a~~ Vinicius, from ~~a~~ Chapecó.*

teacherNotes: Anticipated problem: "I have 28 years" → drill *I'm 28 (years old)*.
Anticipated problem: a/an chosen by letter instead of sound (e.g. "an university") — not triggered by this lesson's vocab set, but flag it as a recurring error to watch for in future situations.

slides.goal: Controlled → freer practice, ending in pair role-play

blocks.label: Task 1 — Complete with am / is / are

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Hi! I ___ Alex, the new intern.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Hi Alex! Welcome! I ___ (your name). Nice to meet you.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Nice to meet you too! ___ you on this team?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, I ___. We ___ a small team, but the projects ___ really cool.

blocks.title: Answer key — Task 1
blocks.body: In order: *am, am, Are, am, are, are, are, am*

blocks.label: Task 2 — a or an?
items: I'm ___ developer.
She's ___ engineer.
He's ___ intern from Canada.
Maria is ___ accountant.
I'm ___ designer on the product team.

blocks.label: Task 3 — Match Alex's questions to the best answers

columns.title: You answer...
rows: c. I'm (name), nice to meet you!
d. I'm from Chapecó, in Santa Catarina.

blocks.label: Task 4 — Build your intro card + role-play
blocks.body:
Write your **intro card**:
- name
- job (*a/an!*)
- team
- city
- one fun fact

In pairs: **Student A = Alex** (use the question card), **Student B = you**. Meet, talk, close politely. Then **swap roles**.

teacherNotes: Anticipated problem: dropped subject — "Is very nice" → *It's very nice*.
Anticipated problem: over-formality — "Hello Mr. Alex, how do you do?" → normalize first names + casual register before the role-play starts.

slides.goal: Live simulated first meeting with Alex, checklist-assessed

blocks.title: Minor Can Do
blocks.body: Get to know Alex and introduce yourself. Alex will ask a few questions and you must answer them.

blocks.label: The task
blocks.body: Alex (teacher or partner) walks up to you. Have a real first conversation — no script in hand.

blocks.label: Success criteria — the student:
blocks.note: **Result:** 4–5 criteria = ✅ Can Do proven · 3 = 🔁 retry after app practice · 0–2 = revisit in office hours
items: Greets Alex and welcomes him to the company
Introduces themselves: name + job (*a/an*) + city, using *to be* correctly
Answers Alex's questions (at least 3)
Asks Alex **at least one** question back
Closes the conversation politely (*Nice meeting you! See you around!*)

blocks.title: Alex's profile card (for the role-play)
blocks.body:
**Alex Miller**, 23, from Vancouver, Canada 🇨🇦
- Marketing intern, 6-month program
- First time in Brazil
- Likes soccer, video games, and coffee
- Speaks slowly and is friendly — a sympathetic interlocutor (A1-appropriate)

**Question bank:** What's your name? · What do you do here? · Where are you from? · How's it going? · Are you from this city? · Is the team big?

teacherNotes: If time is short, cut the question bank to 3 core questions (name, job, city) instead of all 6.

blocks.label: Async app follow-up (this week)
items: Record a 30-second self-introduction (name, job, team, city, fun fact).
Flashcards: greetings + closings set, *to be* forms, *a/an* job titles.
Micro-quiz: choose the best reply to Alex's questions.

teacherNotes: Assign the async tasks live in class so students start within 48h while the lesson is still fresh.
